ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every proposed director, officer, shareholder holding 25% or more of the issued share capital, and every authorized bank signatory against: (i) FINTRAC's domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) and Heads of International Organizations (HIOs) criteria under PCMLTFA Part 1 and SOR/2002-184; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under SEMA, the United Nations Act and FACFCA, including the Special Economic Measures (People's Republic of China) Regulations; (iv) the Criminal Code s. 83.05 terrorist entity list; and (v) the US OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions List, because the ULC's Canadian clearing banks and letter-of-credit issuing banks require OFAC-compatible screening, and the ULC is check-the-box eligible for a US parent. No director or UBO may be a sanctioned person, an adverse-media PEP with unexplained wealth risk, or a person with unresolved regulatory enforcement records. Screening results must be recorded in the corporate KYC file held at the registered office and refreshed annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online filing via authorized Registry Agents using the Corporate Registry System and the federal NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) service provided by Corporations Canada / ISED Canada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of an Alberta ULC must be expressed in Roman/Latin alphabetical characters in English and/or French. Chinese characters are not accepted in the formal registered corporate name. The legal name must therefore employ a transliterated or pinyin brand token (e.g., 'BAIJIU') and must end with the mandatory corporate designation 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'U.L.C.', 'Unlimited Company', or 'UC' prescribed for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation. The Chinese-character trade name may be used commercially and protected separately as a trademark design mark at the Canadian Intellectual Property Office.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan, Deposit, Insurance, Assurance, Finance, Securities, Broker, Brokerage — financial intermediation wording requiring ministerial or financial regulator consent under federal and Alberta statutes
Royal, Crown, Government of Alberta, Canada, Municipality, or any wording falsely implying Crown, governmental or municipal authority
University, College, Institute, School, Academy — educational designations requiring consent or credentialing authorization
Engineer, Engineering, Architect, Architectural — regulated professional titles under the Alberta Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act and Architects Act
Physician, Surgeon, Lawyer, Barrister, Patent Agent, Trademark Agent — regulated professional titles requiring governing-body consent
Co-operative, Condominium, Advertising, Retail Sales — words with statutory evidential or consent requirements
AGLC, Liquor Control Board, or any mark falsely suggesting affiliation with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis agency or a government liquor authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Director of Corporate Registry, the applicant or its corporate/legal agent must file a written reconsideration request with Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must attach a fresh NUANS report, a legal submission distinguishing the cited confusingly similar or prohibited marks under the ABCA name-clearance standard, and, where a sensitive token is involved, the consent letter of the responsible Alberta minister or professional regulator. A second rejection may be challenged by way of judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. If the 90-day name reservation lapses, a new NUANS search and new reservation fee must be submitted before incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The ABCA requires a registered office with a physical street address in Alberta; a post-office box is not permitted. A commercial registered-office suite in Calgary or Edmonton staffed by a licensed corporate services provider is acceptable. A pure virtual mailbox without a staffed physical address is generally not acceptable, and the AGLC liquor wholesale or warehouse licence will in any event require a licensed physical storage or warehouse premise in Alberta. Canadian commercial banks issuing letters of credit will also expect documentary evidence of a physical operating location for the liquor export warehouse.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: low risk — approximately less than 10% probability per annum of an unannounced inspection by Corporate Registry or municipal authorities. AGLC licensed warehouse or wholesale premises: high risk — greater than 40% probability per annum of unannounced compliance inspections by AGLC inspectors, municipal by-law officers or Alberta police. Canada Border Services Agency may additionally conduct unannounced premises examinations for excise and export-compliance purposes.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 2) filed under s. 8 ABCA, accompanied by Form 3 Notice of Directors and Form 4 Notice of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta ULC; shares may be issued without par value and for any lawful consideration. No escrow account is mandated by ABCA, although subscription proceeds committed under the share subscription agreement must be delivered to the Corporation's regulated bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF BAIJIU NATIONAL EXPORT (ALBERTA) ULC: 1. The registered office at Suite 2100, 2500 Sandstone Point, Calgary, Alberta, is adopted for statutory service and recorded with the Alberta Corporate Registry. 3. The following officers are appointed: President, [Officer], and Secretary-Treasurer, [Officer], each vested with signing authority for global trade contracts, bank instructions and liquor import/export filings. 4. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (NUANS name search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary availability search on the Corporate Registry's permitted name database. Submit a formal NUANS name search request for a corporate name that must end with 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'; obtain the Name Search Report and reserve the proposed name for 90 days by referencing it in Article 8 of the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report issued within 90 days of filing
Directors' written consents for the proposed corporate name
Proof of corporate identity of the incorporator or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, queried, or the Name Search Report expires, obtain a new NUANS report and re-submit the name before the registry, or file an alteration of name under s. 13 ABCA after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Governing Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta (pre-filing review by Authorized Service Provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 2 Articles of Incorporation under s. 8 ABCA. Include the unlimited liability statement under s. 5.1, the authorized share structure of one class of unlimited liability shares without par value, and any permitted restrictions on share transfer. Complete Form 3 Notice of Directors and Form 4 Notice of Registered Office. Ensure all first directors sign consents to act in accordance with s. 105 ABCA.
required_dossiers: Form 2 - Articles of Incorporation
Form 3 - Notice of Directors with signed consents
Form 4 - Notice of Registered Office
Consents to Act as Director (s. 105 ABCA)
UBC / interprovincial existence certificate if foreign incorporator is a body corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Director of Corporate Registry queries the articles, amend them under s. 12(1) ABCA and refile within the prescribed correction period; failure to correct will result in rejection and a fresh filing must be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 2, Form 3 and Form 4 through the Alberta Corporate Registry online filing service or a licensed authorized service provider. Pay the CAD 100 statutory incorporation filing fee. Execute parallel notarization of the directors' consents if any director is outside Canada or if the jurisdiction of execution requires apostille authentication.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation (Form 2)
Notice of Directors (Form 3)
Notice of Registered Office (Form 4)
Director consents and identification attestations
CAD 100 statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, correct the stated deficiencies and re-file under s. 12(1) ABCA. A reconsideration request may be submitted to the Registrar within 60 days of the refusal decision, supported by revised dossiers and a fresh Name Search Report if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organizational Meeting and Bylaw Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of BaiJiu National Export (Alberta) ULC; Registrar of Corporations for annual return filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the directors. Adopt By-Law No. 1 addressing share transfers, banking, execution of documents and meeting procedures. Approve the issuance of the 1,000 unlimited liability shares to the subscriber and deliver the corresponding share certificates. Ratify the registered office and officer appointments. Prepare the corporate minute book and register the Corporation's annual return with the Registry within 60 days after each registration anniversary pursuant to s. 113-114 ABCA.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and minutes
By-Law No. 1 adopted in draft
Share certificates and subscription receipts
Register of Directors and Register of Registered Office
Annual Return Form ADR for the initial registry year
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate minute book or annual return is found deficient by the Registrar, file a corrected annual return and pay the late-filing sanction. The directors may amend or replace By-Law No. 1 by ordinary resolution under s. 102 ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Business Number and Federal Tax and Excise Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online and Excise Duty Programs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the ULC for a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online using the Certificate of Incorporation. Activate the corporation tax, GST/HST, payroll and customs accounts. For the export of spirits from Alberta, apply for the appropriate excise license or excise warehouse registration under the Excise Act, 2001, S.C. 2002, c. 22, and register an importer-exporter account with the CBSA for future cross-border transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Alberta)
Form 4 evidence of registered office in Alberta
Board resolution appointing an authorized tax representative
Bank confirmation, letter of credit or exporter evidence for revenue projections
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA does not activate an account within published service standards, submit a BN account reconciliation request through the CRA Business Window and provide the certificate of incorporation and registered office records; if the excise license application is deferred, refrain from physical alcohol storage until formal approval is recorded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Liquor Importation / Exportation Licence and CBSA Export Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC) and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the AGLC for a Liquor Importation Licence or an interprovincial movement authorization if the Baijiu is warehoused in Alberta prior to exportation; obtain a manufacturer's class endorsement only if blending or bottling will occur at the Alberta facility. Register the Corporation with CBSA and obtain a Business Number import/export account; file an export declaration B13A for each shipment of Chinese Baijiu and retain duty-relief evidence under the Excise Act, 2001 for spirits exported from Canada.
required_dossiers: AGLC application for Liquor Importation / Exportation Licence
CBSA export declaration B13A and customs coding
Commercial invoice, bill of lading and letter of credit evidencing the export transaction
Certificate of Incorporation of the ULC
Valid consignee liquor importation permit from the destination country
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CBSA rejects an export declaration, correct and re-submit the declaration through the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal within the statutory correction period. If AGLC raises a compliance query, provide evidence that the spirits are not offered for sale in Alberta and are destined solely for export.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC) for provincial liquor control and Canada Border Services Agency for export declaration control; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for environmental compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: AGLC Liquor Importation/Exportation Licence and CBSA Importer-Exporter Registration under the Excise Act, 2001

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment registration is triggered for an office and warehouse export distribution facility under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12. A Section 68 approval or EPEA registration becomes mandatory if the Alberta facility adds spirit blending, bottling, or bulk ethanol storage capacity above 4,500 L.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No unauthorized wastewater discharge beyond municipal sewer allowances; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions limited to fugitive evaporation from sealed shipping containers and must meet Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (AAQO) and applicable AEPA guidelines. Ethanol spills must be contained and reported in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code and the Storage and Handling of dangerous goods standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code including approved ethanol storage segregation and fire suppression equipment inspection; municipal development permit and building occupancy permit for the Calgary warehouse; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) clearance under the OHS Act, SA 2020, c O-2.2; Workers' Compensation Board - Alberta coverage for warehouse and logistics personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Single federal identifier: CRA Business Number (BN). Core portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO). Provincial registry: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via the Corporate Registry System (CORES). Customs authority: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for the export program account (BN suffixed with 'RD').
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the ULC under the Alberta Business Corporations Act through the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) and obtain the Alberta corporate registry number; 2) File the Alberta Initial Return within 60 days of incorporation; 3) Apply to CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) using BRO or Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number'; 4) Activate the GST/HST account on the BN, selecting the effective registration date and filing frequency (monthly, quarterly or annual as prescribed by CRA); 5) Activate the corporate income tax (Part I T2) account on the BN with a fiscal period-end election; 6) Activate the CBSA customs program account (BN plus 'RD' suffix) for outward shipments; 7) Obtain the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC) liquor wholesale/export authorization, which is a non-tax statutory licence required in parallel to tax registration; 8) Where a US parent intends to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity for US federal tax purposes, file IRS Form 8832 within 75 days of the desired effective date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Default statutory rule under the Income Tax Act (Part I): an Alberta ULC is a separate corporation subject to entity-level taxation. Pass-through status is elective, not automatic. Election mechanisms: (i) Income Tax Act s. 216(1) election, available only where all members/shareholders are resident in Canada, deeming the ULC to be a partnership for income tax purposes; (ii) corresponding deemed-partnership rule under s. 273(1) of the Excise Tax Act for GST/HST purposes once the s. 216(1) election is in force; (iii) hybrid/check-the-box treatment for a US owner: an ABCA ULC is not on the US per se corporation list under Treasury Regulations s. 301.7701-2(b)(8), so IRS Form 8832 may elect disregarded-entity status, supported by the fiscally-transparent rule in Article IV(6)(b) of the Canada-US Tax Treaty (5th Protocol); (iv) anti-hybrid consequences must be tested under ITA s. 18.4 and the Excise Tax Act financial-institution rules, and non-resident shareholders must file prescribed CRA forms for treaty-based relief and withholding analysis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), a value-added tax administered by CRA under the Excise Tax Act. Alberta has no provincial sales tax or HST, so only the 5% federal GST applies to taxable supplies made in Alberta. Complementary indirect duty: Excise Act, 2001 duty on spirits manufactured or imported into Canada, with duty relief for exported spirits via excise warehouse procedures or duty drawback under the Customs Tariff and Customs Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold: a person is not required to register for GST/HST unless the value of taxable supplies made in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter and in the preceding four calendar quarters; exporters of zero-rated goods generally register voluntarily to recover input tax credits; a non-resident person carrying on business in Canada is subject to the same threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no government API clearance for invoice issuance, and no digital stamping regime for B2B invoices. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically (GST NETFILE or CRA My Business Account); voluntary e-invoicing is promoted through the PEPPOL (Pan-European Public Procurement On-Line) framework as the federal standard for electronic exchange. Export controls are effected through CBSA: the B13A Export Declaration or Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) data is submitted to the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform prior to or at export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, a supply of goods made by a GST/HST registrant is zero-rated where the supplier ships or delivers the goods to a destination outside Canada (Part V s. 1) and holds prescribed documentary evidence (ETA s. 22; GST/HST Memorandum 6.3). Services supplied to a non-resident in respect of exported goods, and services performed wholly outside Canada for the benefit of a non-resident, may be zero-rated under Part V ss. 7 and 7.1. Chinese baijiu sold FOB Alberta by the ULC to a foreign buyer therefore attracts GST at 0%; if the baijiu is drop-shipped directly from the PRC supplier to the offshore buyer without entering Canada, the supply is outside the scope of GST/HST rather than zero-rated, and no GST registration is triggered by that supply. Zero-rating requires GST registration to claim input tax credits on warehousing, logistics, and brokerage costs, and the export evidence must exist at the time the net tax return is filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - CBSA Form B13A / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) confirmation or CBSA declaration number (or, for direct PRC drop-shipment, the Chinese customs export declaration)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill or truck Cargo Control Document evidencing physical departure from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation or letter-of-credit presentation documents evidencing receipt of the export sale proceeds
Commercial Invoice and Packing List matching the description, quantity and HS classification (HS 2208.90 for sorghum baijiu spirits)
Export sales contract, purchase order and foreign buyer registration/address evidence proving the foreign destination
AGLC liquor export authorization/waybill and any excise warehouse removal documentation required by the Excise Act, 2001
Carrier proof of delivery at destination (signed delivery receipt or customs entry at destination) supporting the two-year evidentiary window under ETA s. 22
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess the zero-rated supply as taxable at 5% GST, deny the zero-rating claim, claw back related input tax credits, and charge compound interest at the prescribed rate. Knowingly false or grossly negligent export evidence triggers penalties under ETA s. 281 (25% of the tax sought to be evaded), ETA s. 285.1 (gross negligence), summary or indictable prosecution under ETA s. 327, and the ITA s. 163(2) gross negligence penalty (50% of understated income) for parallel income-tax misstatements. False excise-warehouse export claims under the Excise Act, 2001 expose the licensed warehouse and exporter to duty reassessment, seizure, forfeiture and administrative monetary penalties. CRA and CBSA cross-match B13A declarations, carrier records, bills of lading and banking records (including SWIFT MT103s); documentary evidence must be obtained within two years under ETA s. 22 and retained for six years. The 180-day FX repatriation benchmark is a trade-finance and financial-crime compliance covenant (including the PRC SAFE export-proceeds collection rule applicable to the Chinese supply parent) rather than a Canadian federal statutory deadline; however, unrepatriated or misdirected proceeds may be treated by CRA as indicia of a sham export and support a full retrospective clawback plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); cross-border financial intelligence and AML oversight by FINTRAC; export/import and sanctions administration by Global Affairs Canada and applicable federal/ provincial liquor authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains fully free convertibility of both current and capital account transactions under IMF Article VIII. No exchange controls, no prior approval for cross-border transfers, and no statutory restrictions on dividend remittances, loan repatriation, or intercompany payments. A Canadian ULC exporting baijiu may hold foreign currency freely and switch between CAD, USD, CNY-approved offshore pools, EUR, and other currencies. Tax compliance is required, especially Part XIII withholding on non-resident dividends and interest, subject to tax treaty relief under the Canada-China DTA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not mandate surrender, mandatory repatriation, or conversion of export proceeds to CAD. The Export and Import Permits Act imposes licensing and reporting for controlled products, but high-proof sorghum baijiu export is generally not a controlled commodity unless serving embargoed destinations. For accounting and tax purposes, export revenue must be reported in CAD under IFRS and to the CRA using prescribed exchange rates, but there is no obligatory banking conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Canadian law does not provide a standalone EMI license; fintech remittance and multi-currency platforms operate as money services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC and typically partner with Schedule I chartered banks. For an Alberta ULC engaged in baijiu export, a fintech EMI may be used as a secondary collection or disbursement rail, but it cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, provide trade finance, or act as a primary capital escrow facility. Offshore EMIs not registered as MSBs in Canada are legally barred from active solicitation and are unusable for the ULC's principal business.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Schedule I banks require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to complete an in-person interview at an Alberta branch before account activation. While the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act allows certain remote ID verification methods, major banks generally exercise discretion to require physical presence for non-resident-controlled ULCs. Remote opening is occasionally granted only after enhanced due diligence and a credible third-party identity verification threshold; otherwise, directors must attend a physical branch meeting with original passports, proof of residential address, corporate attestation, and beneficial ownership declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder control and ULC unlimited-liability pass-through status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial certified copy of Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) ULC Articles of Incorporation, certificate of status, corporate minute book extract, UBO registry declaration with detailed corporate chain, personal identification for all directors and shareholders, tax residency certificates, audited source-of-wealth statement signed by the UBO, and a legal opinion confirming unlimited liability implications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-proof alcoholic beverage export triggering regulated liquor licensing and sanctions-risk review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Alberta AGLC Liquor Wholesale/Import/Export license (where applicable), federal and provincial excise registrations, product labels and composition certificates, ISO 22000/food safety certificates, export destination and end-user letters, USOFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening results, and a detailed compliance policy covering prohibited trade partners and dual-use categories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to Chinese baijiu distilleries with associated trade-based money laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase contracts, commercial invoices showing shipment-specific price, bill of lading, packing lists, HS code classifications (2208.90 for baijiu), China Customs export declarations, quality inspection certificates, independent valuation report aligned to open-market prices, and a certified statement of, related-party ownership with the Chinese supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Over/under-invoicing or third-party payment mismatch in import/export transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full audit trail of goods movement: marine/ocean bill of lading, freight invoices, insurance certificates, terminal receipts, customs bonded warehouse receipts, warehouse-out records, sales ledger with matching SWIFT references, third-party payment authorization resolutions, and contractual anti-fraud clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore jurisdiction considered high-risk by the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement of the transferring institution, source of funds documentation evidencing lawful acquisition (e.g., audited financial statements, board minutes approving dividend/distribution, sale agreement and transfer taxes paid), share subscription agreement on paid-up capital, stamp duty and corporate registry filings, and a confirmation from an independent legal counsel on compliance with applicable foreign exchange controls of the investor's jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the foreign shareholder to the ULC's CAD/USD operational account. Use bank purpose code corresponding to 'Foreign Direct Investment' and in field 70 include 'ULC Share Subscription / Capital Injection / [Alberta Corporate Registry Number]'. For transfers originating from the PRC, the Chinese shareholder must obtain SAFE FDI registration for outbound investment and route through a Chinese-designated bank; the Canadian side must provide a copy of the ABCA ULC filing, board resolution, share subscription agreement, and proof of beneficial ownership. FINTRAC reporting applies if the transaction is $10,000 CAD or more, and the bank will conduct enhanced due diligence for non-resident shareholder funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails for baijiu trade are an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (L/C) issued by the ULC's Canadian bank to the Chinese supplier under ICC UCP600, transmitted via SWIFT MT700, with settlement by MT103/MT202 at sight. For global customer collections, use direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from foreign importers to the ULC account; alternatively, documentary collection under D/P or D/A terms with a collection instruction to the presenting bank. All trade invoices must reference the relevant L/C number, bill of lading, HS code, and excise permit to allow bank compliance and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-Currency Swap (CAD vs CNY or USD)
Vanilla FX Options (put/call on CAD, USD, or CNY)
Structured forward with barrier feature (subject to bank credit and suitability approval)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (ABCA s. 133)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 year-end, due by January 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late fee (approx. USD 75) on filing after the deadline; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years permits the Registrar to dissolve the company by administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 (the standard AGLC licence expiry/renewal date; renewal notice issued 60 days in advance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal may require a reinstatement fee; failure to renew results in automatic licence lapse and an immediate stop-order on liquor export activity; continued unlicensed operation triggers AGLC compliance action, monetary penalties, and licence revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for private Alberta ULCs under ABCA unless requisitioned by shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares (s. 153(4)) or required by AGLC as a condition of liquor export/wholesale licence; a unanimous shareholder resolution may waive auditor appointment in each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (if not publicly accountable) or IFRS; a ULC may elect either framework under CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS becomes mandatory if the entity is a reporting issuer.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not yet impose a separate statutory beneficial-ownership confirmation filing under the ABCA. The ULC must maintain current internal books on share transfers and significant individuals for AML due diligence, review and ratify the register annually at the shareholders' meeting, and update within 15 days of any transfer or control change. The annual registry return confirms only directors and registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Available incentives include the federal SR&ED tax credit (not applicable to non-CCPC ULCs), investment tax credits for clean technology, and the Alberta Innovation Employment Grant; none materially reduce the 23% combined federal (15%) and Alberta (8%) corporate tax rate for export wholesale.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) or through EFILE-approved tax preparation software; mandatory electronic filing applies to most corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly instalment payments of corporate income tax when combined federal/provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 6 months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., a December 31 year-end must be filed by June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered address, 15-character Business Number (BN), taxation year-end, and fiscal period commencement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC owned by a non-resident, insert the Alberta registered address, the active BN, and attach Schedule 17 listing the Chinese parent as ultimate owner with country code CN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for tax purposes after all adjustments, including non-deductible provisions and permitted loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income from global export sales as taxable in Canada; any intercompany purchases of baijiu from related Chinese suppliers must be recorded at arm's length under section 247 and supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at the 15% general corporate rate on taxable income, reduced by applicable federal tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No exemption for export revenues; the full 15% federal rate applies unless a specific federal credit (e.g., investment tax credit) is available to the ULC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta income tax at 8% general corporate rate, after provincial tax credits and loss carryover adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Form T2114 to allocate taxable income to Alberta; for a centralized ULC with its only permanent establishment in Alberta, allocate 100% to Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies all shareholders, including non-resident persons and corporations, and their share ownership percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Chinese parent corporate name, Chinese tax identification number, registered address, and shareholding percentage; this schedule supports treaty withholding claims for future dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under subsection 162(1): 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full calendar month of delay, to a maximum of 12 months; a minimum $100 penalty applies even if no tax is owing. Gross negligence penalty under subsection 163(2): 50% of the understated tax. Late payment interest accrues daily at the prescribed rate compound.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act; reduced under the Canada-China DTA to 15% generally and to 10% for dividends paid to a Chinese company holding at least 10% of the voting shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Chinese beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Residence from the Chinese tax authority and provide it, together with a completed CRA Form NR301 (or NR302/NR303 for corporate shareholders), to the Canadian ULC before the dividend is paid. The payor retains these documents for six years; if the 25% domestic rate was withheld, a refund application via the T196 form is made to the CRA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for both royalties and interest. Under the Canada-China DTA, the rate is 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and any applicable limitation-of-benefit clause in the relevant protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate per transaction class with any non-arm's length non-resident; triggers mandatory T106 information return and contemporaneous Local File/Master File preparation. Master File is required where the MNE group's consolidated gross revenue exceeds CAD 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The CRA applies the general anti-avoidance rule (subsection 245(2)) and the transfer-pricing substance-over-form provisions in section 247. For a ULC, corporate residence and separate legal personality will be respected only where substantive economic activities exist in Canada: a physical office, qualified employees exercising decision-making autonomy, genuine commercial risk, and real business purpose. Lack of such substance may lead the CRA to recharacterize the ULC as a conduit or sham, reallocating income to the Chinese parent and denying treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting export sales revenues, fabricating purchase invoices from Chinese suppliers, or destroying books and records related to the Baijiu wholesale distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable offence under section 239 of the Income Tax Act; imprisonment up to 5 years and fines between 50% and 200% of the evaded tax; gross negligence civil penalty of 50% plus compound interest; loss of loss carryforward rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly directed or participated are jointly and severally liable, subject to criminal fines, imprisonment, civil restitution to the CRA, and travel bans or asset freezes under subsection 224.1 to prevent leaving Canada without satisfying outstanding tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling Baijiu to related Chinese trading affiliates at excessive cost or intercompany margins inconsistent with the arm's length standard, failing to maintain transfer pricing documentation, or failing to file the T106 information return for transactions exceeding CAD 1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may redetermine taxable income using the CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split methodology; subsection 247(3) imposes a penalty of 10% of the net upward adjustment where the adjustment exceeds CAD 5 million; interest and reclassification of funds as shareholder distributions with Part XIII withholding exposure also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held liable under section 227.1 for unremitted Part XIII withholding arising from reclassified dividends; signing a false T106 or transferring pricing report may result in personal penalties; CRA travel bans apply in cases of egregious non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ULC as a shell with no physical Alberta office, no local employees, no independent commercial functions, and booking export sales in Canada solely to gain treaty benefits and defer Chinese CFC tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can invoke GAAR to disregard the entity or reallocate the income to the Chinese parent for failure of the economic substance test; denial of treaty benefits under the beneficial ownership clause; possible application of global minimum tax (under Pillar Two) leading to top-up taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the court pierces the corporate veil, the Chinese parent's directors can be assessed as carrying on the Canadian business directly under section 142, with retroactive tax liability and personal liability for amounts outstanding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to the Chinese parent without withholding the required statutory or treaty rate and without filing the NR4 information return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Canadian payor is liable for the full unwithheld amount under section 215; a 10% penalty is imposed under subsection 227(10) plus daily compound interest at the prescribed rate; NR4 late filing penalties up to CAD 100 per day apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under subsection 227.1(1) if they were aware of or caused the failure to withhold; CRA may assess directors personally and freeze personal bank accounts and property until the outstanding withholding tax is paid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume SWIFT wires and letters of credit without FINTRAC registration, failing to maintain trade invoices and bills of lading reconciliation, or engaging in over-invoicing/under-invoicing Baijiu exports to move illicit funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative penalties up to CAD 500,000 per violation for corporations; under the Criminal Code, money laundering is an indictable offence punishable by up to 14 years of imprisonment; trade document falsification carries separate criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly authorize or endorse laundering transactions can be criminally prosecuted, subject to fines, imprisonment, travel bans for ongoing proceedings, asset forfeiture, and personal civil liability for damages.
